findings.what: The newly supplied func_015b66 definition returns int and its decoy caller tests the full result, but its two existing external consumers still declare it void. This newly exposed cross-unit return-type mismatch is avoidable, not a preserved original bug. In addition, the two new item units declare int abs while the expressly corrected elevator_scene and its transition neighbor use long abs; these have the same width in MCC68K but remain different C declarations. All consistent-return alternatives reproduce both revisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Move func_015b66 out of the void declaration lists into extern int declarations in both callers. alternatives/int-effect-call/player_states_and_respawn.c MATCHes all seven functions and alternatives/int-effect-telephone/telephone.c MATCHes all three, both revisions. Prefer extern long abs() in the two new item units, as independently matching alternatives/long-abs-setup/ and alternatives/long-abs-updates/ demonstrate. This does not by itself reconcile older abs declarations elsewhere.

findings.what: The new map icon unit declares ELEVATOR_LOCATION as an array of sixteen-byte elevator_state records, absorbing each actual secondary eight-byte elevator record into reserved[10]. Existing elevator files declare the same object as eight-byte elevator_record pairs, ELEVATOR_LOCATION[][2]. The chosen stride yields correct bytes and is not an address trick, but creates an avoidable incompatible extern view and hides the already known paired layout.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse struct elevator_record { short x, y; char level, state, entity, timer; }, declare ELEVATOR_LOCATION[][2], and select &ELEVATOR_LOCATION[elevator_number][0]. The complete private alternative alternatives/paired-elevator-record/elevator_icon.c independently MATCHes both revisions without casts or compiler options.

findings.what: The new pickup routine's signed-long view of the shared unsigned flags field and the timer's (&gPlayerInfo[player])->sprite_state spelling are matching-sensitive choices disclosed in the author handoff but not locally in source, repeating the kind of honesty qualification just fixed for C012 F4. The tested plain alternatives fail: cast removal saves four emitted bytes; direct timer indexing saves four, and a local pointer saves ten. Also, the timer comment describes twelve-/two-tick bit intervals, but the packet performs timer & 12 and timer & 2: 12 and 2 are masks, not blink periods.
findings.suggested_fix: Add brief local compiler-choice qualifications explaining the observed signed-value mask exchanges and address-of/index schedule while keeping common storage unsigned; label exact historical spelling unknown [INFERENCE]. Correct the timer comment to describe masks 12 and 2 near expiration rather than implying twelve-/two-tick periods. No behavioral fix, pointer cast or shared-type change is needed. Retained experimental sources/listings are under alternatives/unsigned-flags/, alternatives/direct-player-index/ and alternatives/timer-player-pointer/.
